name: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces
problem: Subquadratic alternatives to attention (linear attention, gated convolution, recurrent models, SSMs) matched Transformers poorly on discrete data because they could not do content-based reasoning: their recurrence was input-independent, so the model could not choose what to keep.
mechanism: Makes the SSM parameters functions of the input, which is the whole contribution. The layer is a selective SSM: input x is projected to (delta, B, C) where delta_t = softplus(W_delta x_t + bias) is data-dependent, B_t and C_t are data-dependent, and the state updates h_t = exp(delta_t * A) h_{t-1} + delta_t * B_t x_t^T followed by y_t = C_t h_t + D x_t. Because B, C and delta now depend on the token, the model can selectively propagate or forget along sequence length per input, which is what earlier fixed-parameter SSMs (S4) could not do. Selectivity rules out the fast causal convolution used before, so decoding uses a hardware-aware parallel scan rather than a naive sequential recurrence. The block is a single residual path with no attention and no MLP: essentially Mamba block = gated conv1d shortcut + selective SSM, pre-norm residual. The state is a fixed-size (batch, d_inner, d_state) tensor per layer, CONSTANT in sequence length, so there is NO KV cache at all: per-token decode cost is O(d_model * d_state) state bytes instead of O(2 * L * d_h * d_k) KV bytes. That is the defining serving consequence and the reason long-context SSM decoding does not degrade with context length.
speedup_reported: 5x higher inference throughput than Transformers, against the paper's own GPT-3-style Transformer baselines at matched size; Mamba-3B matches Transformers twice its size in pretraining and downstream evaluation, and performance improves up to million-token sequences. The throughput figure is the authors' own reference implementation on A100 GPUs with their custom kernels and is not a tuned-engine number; published 5x claims for Mamba have consistently shrunk once engines run the model with generic PyTorch rather than the fused scan.
notes:
The single most consequential SSM paper: it made input-dependent recurrence work well enough to scale to billions of parameters, and everything downstream (Mamba-2, Jamba, Zamba, Falcon Mamba, Granite 4.0, Kimi Linear, Qwen3-Next) is either Mamba or a hybrid with it. CRITICAL serving caveat: the state is constant-size so the KV cache is eliminated, but the per-step update is a SEQUENTIAL scan in the time dimension that tensor cores do not accelerate, so decode becomes latency-bound on the scan kernel rather than bandwidth-bound on weights. This is why Mamba-style models need hand-written scan kernels to be fast and why naive implementations disappoint. Verified supported: vLLM has native MambaForCausalLM and Mamba2ForCausalLM rows; llama.cpp has LLM_ARCH_MAMBA and LLM_ARCH_MAMBA2 and lists mamba in llm_arch_is_recurrent(). Engine support is real but was late and the open issue trackers show continuing kernel work (llama.cpp 'metal: optimize Mamba-2 SSM scan decode' open; vLLM has multiple open Mamba kernel PRs).
